name: The Bail Project (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: people bailed out or supported pretrial at The Bail Project's US sites, and their families.
summary: The Bail Project pays bail for people in US jails who can't afford it, through a revolving fund to which about nine in ten bail dollars return, and supports them until their cases close; its bail line cost about $9.7 million with overhead and the year's lost bail in the year to June 2025, for about 3,300 bailouts and 2,100 people supported without bail in community-release pilots. Each bailout is counted as the charity's own yearly days of pretrial detention prevented over its bailouts, about 25 days, 60% of them days really saved, plus fewer convictions and sentences, better employment later, homes kept, clients' fines paid and county jail costs, valued with the site's shared figures for time in jail; most of the value is the deaths that time in jail causes, taken from a study of prison terms at half the rate for weeks in jail. The result is about {{result}} years of healthy life per 1,000 dollars: a few weeks out of jail for about {{row:cost_per_bailout}} a bailout (the pilots, which do little measurable good, sharing the cost), valued on a scale where help for the world's poorest goes much further. The biggest uncertainties are how many deaths a few weeks in jail cause, how much of the counted detention clients would have served anyway, and the year's bailouts, which the charity doesn't publish; the whole model is discounted for missing data, and a gift waits about three years behind the charity's reserves.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

output.label: Years of healthy life per dollar you give

story.sentence: Every **{cost_total / people_reached|$}** pays bail and support for one person who cannot afford it, so they wait for trial at home.

rows.label: Programme service expenses, fiscal 2025 (July 2024 to June 2025)

source.title: The Bail Project, Form 990 for July 2024 to June 2025 (ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer, EIN 81-4985512; IRS e-file 202620619349300142 in the IRS bulk archive 2026_TEOS_XML_03A.zip)
source.quote: Total functional expenses: program service expenses 10,270,968
source.note: Part I line 18 total expenses 13,872,645; Schedule D Part XII reconciles to audited total expenses of 16,254,891, adding a 2,284,937 'loss on uncollectible pledges, loans and bail receivables' and 97,309 of donated services. The 990 reports one programme.

rows.explainer: All four of the charity's programmes (bail assistance and client support, policy advocacy, public education, research), from the audited return for the latest year with audited spending and reach. The bail loss the auditors recognised is a catch-up of several years, so this model counts the year's own lost bail instead (bail_lost below).

rows.label: Total expenses, fiscal 2025

source.title: The Bail Project, Form 990 for July 2024 to June 2025 (ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer, EIN 81-4985512; IRS e-file 202620619349300142 in the IRS bulk archive 2026_TEOS_XML_03A.zip)

rows.explainer: Programme expenses plus management and general ($2,602,698) and fundraising ($998,979), before the bail loss and donated services that the audited statements add.

rows.label: Share of programme expenses on bail assistance and client support
rows.explainer: The shared split for fiscal 2025 (62%, from fiscal 2024's published split), read also by the advocacy model so the two add to the programme.

rows.label: Bail assistance and client support, fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: Paying bail through the national revolving fund, the Bail Disruptors who meet clients in jail and court, reminders, rides, referrals, the community-release pilots and grants to partner bail funds ($509,730). About $6.4 million.

rows.label: Overhead ratio (total ÷ programme expenses)
rows.explainer: Management and fundraising spread over every programme by its cost.

rows.label: Bail paid in fiscal 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: The year's bailouts at the charity's average bail: about $10 million.

rows.label: Bail not returned from the year's bailouts (US$)
rows.explainer: Forfeited after missed dates or kept for fines and fees: 11% of the year's bail, about $1.1 million, the money the revolving fund really uses up on these cases. The rest returns and pays the next bail. The bail out in the courts (about $11 million at June 2025) is an asset; its forgone interest is left out, cost being the charity's own spending (Convention 2).

rows.label: Full cost of bail assistance and client support, fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: The bail line with its share of overhead, plus the year's lost bail: about $9.7 million.

rows.label: Clients served in fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: The change in the charity's cumulative count (the shared fact): {{row:clients_fy2025}} people, bailed out or supported in the pilots.

rows.label: Days of pretrial detention the charity counts as prevented in fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: The change in its cumulative count (the shared fact): 81,732 days, read as gross.

rows.label: Days of pretrial detention avoided per bailout (the charity's estimate)
rows.explainer: The year's days over the year's bailouts: about 25 days (the cumulative average since 2018 is 40, from longer holds in the early years). Read as gross, the days clients would have been held had nobody paid; release by other means is counted once, in counterfactual_adj. Clients' cases take a median six months to close.

rows.label: People bailed out in fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: The shared estimate: cumulative bailouts at June 2025 (34,572) less the more than 31,000 to June 2024, {{row:bailouts_fy2025}} (3,050 to 3,570). The year's bail dollars aren't usable (the reports give $91 million in both years).

rows.label: People supported without bail (community-release pilots), fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: The year's other clients, about 2,100: people released without bail in Illinois (which ended cash bail in September 2023), Washtenaw County and St. Louis, given court reminders, rides and referrals.

rows.label: Household size (poorest fifth of US households)
rows.explainer: The service is to one person, so households here only carry the count: households_reached is clients over this size and people_reached multiplies it back. Effects on clients' families are a side effect below.

rows.label: Clients' households
rows.explainer: Clients over household size, so that people_reached is the year's clients.

rows.label: Clients served, fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: The year's clients: bailouts and pilot clients.

rows.label: Cost per client
rows.explainer: About {{row:cost_per_person}} a client.

rows.label: Cost per bailout, all cost on bailouts
rows.explainer: Context: about $2,900 a bailout if the pilots cost nothing; they share the cost in the model.

rows.label: Days of post-conviction jail or prison avoided per bailout
rows.explainer: The shared figure for a defendant released rather than detained (Heaton et al. 2017; Dobbie et al. 2016): 12 days (0 to 45). The sentences come after the case closes, a median six months.

rows.label: Median time for a client's case to close (months)
rows.explainer: The wait before a sentence avoided would have begun.

rows.label: Years of sentence avoided per bailout, discounted
rows.explainer: After the case closes, at the shared rate.

rows.label: Years of incarceration avoided per bailout, discounted
rows.explainer: Pretrial days now plus sentence days later: about 0.1 years.

rows.label: Fall in missed court dates from reminders (share of defendants)

source.title: Science News on Fishbane, Ouss and Shah (2020), Behavioral nudges reduce failure to appear for court, Science 370
source.quote: almost 38 percent of individuals in the control group missed their court dates, compared with just below 30 percent of those receiving text messages

rows.explainer: In New York City's randomised trial, text reminders cut missed dates by about 8 points for people summoned for low-level offences. Pilot clients are released by the courts anyway, so the reminders are the part that keeps them out of jail: 8 points (3 to 12).

rows.label: Days in jail after a missed court date
rows.explainer: The shared judgment: 5 days (1 to 20) held on a warrant after a missed date.

rows.label: Years of incarceration avoided per pilot client
rows.explainer: Missed dates avoided times the days each brings: under half a day.

rows.label: Years of incarceration avoided per client (weighted)
rows.explainer: Bailouts' and pilot clients' years averaged over the clients; within a year, so not discounted again.

rows.label: Life satisfaction lost per year in jail or prison (points)
rows.explainer: The site's shared figure ({{row:ls_gain_per_person_year}} points, 0.5 to 3), read by every model that counts incarceration avoided.

rows.label: WELLBYs per client, discounted
rows.explainer: Incarceration's life satisfaction over the years avoided, plus the homes bailed-out clients keep (the shared share, loss and time to rehouse).

rows.label: Formal earnings gained per released defendant a year (US$)
rows.explainer: The site's shared figure from Dobbie, Goldin and Yang's judge-assignment study: $500 a year (0 to 2,000), mostly from fewer convictions; jobs lost in detention are in it.

rows.label: Clients' fines and fees paid from bail not returned, per bailout (US$)
rows.explainer: The part of the lost bail courts keep for fines and fees the client would otherwise owe: a one-off gain to the client, about $170.

rows.label: Earnings gained per client a year (US$)
rows.explainer: Bailed-out clients' gain spread over all clients; pilot clients are released anyway and gain nothing here.

rows.label: US household spending per person (Consumer Expenditure Survey, 2024)
rows.explainer: The site's one US survey consumption figure.

rows.label: Clients' consumption per person as a share of the US mean
rows.explainer: People who can't pay a $3,000 bail are poor: the poorest fifth's spending share, per household, turned into per person with the shared household sizes.

rows.label: Clients' consumption per person (US$ a year)
rows.explainer: The base the gains are measured against on the site's log scale.

rows.label: How long released defendants' better employment holds (years)
rows.explainer: The shared figure: 4 years (2 to 10).

rows.label: Gain in ln(consumption) per client, discounted
rows.formula: ln(1 + value_per_person / baseline_consumption) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, income_years) + bailouts_fy2025 / people_reached * ln(1 + fees_paid_per_bailout / baseline_consumption)
rows.explainer: The yearly earnings gain on the site's log scale over the years it lasts, discounted, plus the one-off fees paid for the client.

rows.label: Jail costs a county saves per day a person isn't held (US$)
rows.explainer: The shared marginal cost of a jail day, {{row:jail_cost_per_day}} (15 to 80), below the $77 average the charity's own savings figure implies.

rows.label: Public money saved or received per client (US$)
rows.formula: (bailouts_fy2025 * bail_detention_years + pilot_clients_fy2025 * pilot_detention_years) * 365 * jail_cost_per_day / people_reached + bailouts_fy2025 / people_reached * @the_bail_project.average_bail * (1 - @the_bail_project.bail_revolved_share) * (1 - @the_bail_project.fees_share_of_bail_kept)
rows.explainer: Jail and sentence days not paid for (the sentence days discounted), and the forfeited bail counties keep.

rows.label: Value of the public money per client (units of value)
rows.explainer: Counties' money is worth what it spares their taxpayers: on the site's log scale, a dollar over consumption per person (the household survey's mean, the clients' scale), times the shared cost of public funds over how state and local taxes fall.

rows.label: Deaths per year of pretrial jail, as a share of the shared prison figure
rows.explainer: The shared judgment: half the prison rate per year (0.1 to 1.2), the time inside priced pro rata and lowered because deaths in jail cluster in the first days, before bail is posted.

rows.label: Deaths averted per client
rows.explainer: Years incarcerated avoided times the shared years of life lost per year, as a share of the remaining life of a person inside (40 years), at jail's share, discounted for the years until the deaths come.

rows.label: Share of deaths averted under five
rows.explainer: Clients are adults charged with crimes.

rows.label: Share aged 5-14 of deaths over five
rows.explainer: No clients under 18.

rows.label: Share aged 15-49 of deaths over fifteen
rows.explainer: The clients' ages (the shared figure, {{row:share_15_49_of_over15}}).

rows.label: Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: GiveWell's moral weights by the age band of each death, times your value of a life: the site's one value of a death.

rows.label: Healthy years from illness averted per client
rows.explainer: Illness in jail and after is in the shared life-satisfaction and mortality figures; nothing is counted twice here.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (validity of the shared release effects)
rows.explainer: The shared validity figure for these clients: 0.75 (0.5 to 0.95), as Prison Policy Initiative's decarceration branch.

rows.label: Share of the detention clients would really have served without the charity
rows.explainer: Release by other means (family, a bondsman, another bail fund, a judge's review, a guilty plea), counted only here: 60% of the charity's gross days (35% to 95%). The same share applies to pilot clients, whom courts and public defenders also remind.

rows.label: The charity's share of the resources behind the release
rows.explainer: The bail and support are the charity's (grants to partner bail funds are in its cost); partner sites' own staff and donated services ($97,309 in fiscal 2025) are the rest. Public defenders' work is the case, not the release.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Share of the value kept after missed court dates
rows.explainer: Clients make 92% of their court dates; a missed date costs some days held again on a warrant, not the earnings or sentences: about 0.98.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: The shared figure: 0.95 (0.85 to 1.05).

rows.label: Years until a donation is spent
rows.explainer: At June 2025 the charity held $44.8 million in cash, savings and investments (Form 990 for fiscal 2025, end-of-year balance sheet) beside $11.3 million of bail out in the courts, against spending of $14-16 million a year, and it is spending down: a $9.4 million deficit in fiscal 2025, 'intentionally operated at a budgeted deficit'. A gift now is spent when reserves run low: our judgment, 3 years (1 to 5).

rows.label: Discount for the wait until a gift is spent
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate over the wait above.

rows.label: Missing outcome data
rows.explainer: Thin: the year's bailouts are estimated from cumulative counts and the effect comes from studies of release by lenient judges, not of the charity's clients; its own outcome data (court return, dismissals) aren't against a comparison group. So the site's discount for missing data applies.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Side effect: children and partners spared a parent's detention, as a share of the value
rows.explainer: The shared figure: {{row:ue_family}} (0 to 30%).

rows.label: Side effect: crime by clients while released, net of crime later avoided, as a share of the value
rows.explainer: The shared figure: {{row:ue_crime}} (-20% to +5%), against Prison Policy Initiative's -10% for people kept out of prison for years.

rows.label: Side effects, as a share of the value
rows.explainer: The two side effects above, each read through the side-effect weight.

rows.label: Income gained, public money saved and deaths averted, in GiveWell units of value (before adjustments)
Income gained and deaths averted, in healthy years
rows.explainer: The bridge from UoV into healthy years (docs/normalization.md 2.6): fixed, don't edit.

rows.label: Life satisfaction gained, in wellbeing-adjusted life years (before adjustments)
Life satisfaction gained, in healthy years
rows.explainer: The bridge from WELLBYs into healthy years (docs/normalization.md 2.6): fixed, don't edit.

rows.label: Healthy years counted directly (before adjustments)
Years of healthy life
rows.explainer: Every outcome, each in healthy years by its own unit's conversion, times the adjustments.

rows.label: Years of healthy life per dollar
Salaries, compensation and benefits, fiscal 2025

rows.explainer: Staff pay across the organisation, from the audited return.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs
rows.explainer: Bail Disruptors are hired locally, many with experience of the system: the shared gap for delivery staff hired locally.
